processSection.heading: How we build your website
processSection.subtitle: Four steps. You see the design before anything is built.

steps.title: Plan (a few days)
steps.description: We agree what the site must do, who it's for and what goes on each page.

steps.title: Design (about a week)
steps.description: You see how it looks on a phone and a computer, and we refine it until you approve.

steps.title: Build (one to two weeks)
steps.description: We build the site, connect your forms and payments, and set it up for Google.

steps.title: Launch and support (30 days)
steps.description: We test everything, put it live, show you how to update it, and fix anything for 30 days.

pricingSection.heading: Website prices

pricingSection.note: Prices are starting points. The final price depends on the number of pages, payments and how much writing you need, and you get it in writing before any work starts.

faqSection.heading: Common questions
faqSection.subtitle: What people ask before starting a website with us.

faqs.question: How long does a website take?
faqs.answer: A one-page website takes about a week. A 5-page business website takes about 3 weeks. Online shops and web apps take 6 to 12 weeks, planned in phases. The biggest factor is how quickly we get your content and feedback.

faqs.question: What do you build on?
faqs.answer: Whatever suits the job. Business websites use modern, fast tools with a simple system to edit your content. Online shops can use Shopify or a custom build. You own every account.

faqs.question: Do I need to provide the words and photos?
faqs.answer: No. If you have them, we use them. If not, we write the words and prepare the images for an extra fee.

faqs.question: Will it work on phones?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every site is designed for phones first, then tablets and computers.

faqs.question: What happens after launch?
faqs.answer: You get 30 days of fixes and small changes. After that, you can update it yourself or choose a monthly plan for updates, backups and reporting.

faqs.question: Can you handle a large project?
faqs.answer: Yes. Large websites, online shops and web apps are planned in phases. Each phase has a fixed price, a timeline and your sign-off, and you follow progress in your client portal. We built Omek's online store and the system that runs it.
